findings.summary: samePath folds backslashes but not a leading "./", so a decisions entry or a baseline survivor spelled "./src/cart.ts" silently fails to match the bare spelling; still open, and the divergence is still unrecorded at samePath.
findings.evidence:
Re-probed on this candidate tree (src/qa-probe.test.ts, added and removed in this disposable worktree; `pnpm vitest run src/qa-probe.test.ts`).

Decisions side — one survivor id "1" file "src/cart.ts", one ACCEPT entry with the same id and the file spelled four ways:
  "src/cart.ts"     -> accepted
  "./src/cart.ts"   -> unattributed
  "  src/cart.ts  " -> accepted
  "src\\cart.ts"     -> accepted

Baseline side — same defect through the other key: a parsed baseline holding the same location under file "./src/cart.ts":
  baseline "./src/cart.ts" vs survivor "src/cart.ts" -> new-in-this-run (expected pre-existing)

Root cause is one function, shared by both keys: src/mutation-report.ts:445-447 `samePath` is `file.replace(/\\/g, "/")` — the backslash half of the already-exported `normalizeWaiverPath` (src/afk-manifest.ts:146-148, `value.trim().replace(/\\/g, "/").replace(/^(?:\.\/)+/, "")`), with the `./` strip dropped. `baselineKey` (:465) and `decisionKey` (:490) both call it. The whitespace half of round 1's clear condition is now met, but by the decisions parser rather than by `samePath`: `parseMutationDecisions` trims every string field (src/mutation-report.ts:374), which is why "  src/cart.ts  " resolves. The `./` half is unmet on both keys.

Neither alternative in the clear condition holds on this tree: `git log -p` since 2a7c983 shows no change to `samePath` since round 1, its doc comment ("One spelling for a path, so a baseline and a report compare the same bytes") records no deliberate divergence, and no test asserts the `./` spelling — `grep -n '\./' src/mutation-report.test.ts` returns only import specifiers.
findings.expected: The contract fixes the two match keys (B-05 location-and-mutator, B-07 id-corroborated-by-file) and mandates no path normalization, so partial tolerance is inside the contract. But `samePath` exists precisely to fold one path-spelling difference, which sets the expectation that path shape is tolerated — and `afk.json`'s own baselinePath and decisionsPath do go through `normalizeWaiverPath`, so the manifest tolerates `./` where the artifacts' own file members do not.
findings.observed: A `./`-prefixed `file` resolves nothing on either key: the ACCEPT entry keeps its survivor at the baseline label, or a genuinely pre-existing survivor is reported new-in-this-run, and no note is produced, so the operator gets no signal that their spelling matched nothing. Harm stays bounded exactly as B-07 and B-12 describe and as the ship-gate test at src/ship-gate.test.ts:2577 proves: one report bullet, read by no gate, verdict or PR-open condition, with the survivor still in the list at full detail.
findings.clearCondition: A decisions entry or baseline survivor whose `file` differs from the survivor's only by a leading `./` resolves to the same identity as the bare spelling, with a test asserting the resulting label for that spelling — or the divergence is recorded at `samePath` as a deliberate choice.
